title: Choose the visual world for the eATL site
question: The roll assigned the Split-Flap Ops Board. Keep it, take an alternate, or re-roll.

options.label: Split-Flap Ops Board
options.thesis: Every ATL record is a row on a split-flap board; scrolling flips it from blank to signed and closed.
options.viewport: A wall-sized board: the parked aircraft assembled from flap tiles, YU-RDA-000001 clattering in above one line and a CONTACT flap row.
options.risk: Split-flap is a known airport trope; it fails if it reads as a novelty font instead of a governing grid.

raised.raise: Status rows flip whole flap fields to flat colour (yellow DEFERRED, red BLOCKED, green CLOSED), never neon dots on black.
System states print themselves on the board (SIGN BLOCKED: 2 FIELDS MISSING) instead of appearing as UI chrome.
One strict flap-cell grid governs the entire page, captions and nav included.

options.label: The Technical Log Sheet
options.thesis: The page is the ATL sheet itself: scroll and the aircraft's flight writes itself into the form, then signs, hashes and peels its copies.
options.viewport: A giant ATL page, plan-view aircraft drawn in its header box, fields filling in ballpoint as you scroll; canary and pink copies offset beneath.
options.risk: The literal reading of your brief and where most runs would land; can feel quaint if the paper is soft instead of forensic.

options.label: Timetable Slide Rack
options.lineage: 1970s pocket airline timetables on a light table
options.thesis: eATL as a raked rack of tinted timetable slides on a lit goldenrod bed, one type size, rank by weight and reversal.
options.viewport: Raked slides carrying the ATL sections, one light sweeping along the rake as you scroll.
options.case: Strong airline identity and a rare form; loses on clarity because one type size fights a loud animated landing page.
options.risk: Reads as heritage airline nostalgia rather than a compliance product.

options.label: Solidarity Silkscreen
options.thesis: One emblematic aircraft in flat fearless ink with a running multilingual border.
options.viewport: A centred emblem with the slogan circling the edges.
options.case: Operators do not identify with political poster language; a compliance product loses clarity.
options.risk: Political connotation unrelated to aviation records.
options.kept: Total flat-colour commitment for status fields.

options.label: Phosphor Terminal
options.thesis: The log as a live transcript on green phosphor.
options.viewport: An 80-column transcript printing a flight record.
options.case: Reads as developer tooling, not cockpit paperwork; the near-black neon rut.
options.kept: System states print themselves rather than appearing as chrome.

options.label: ASCII Live Render
options.thesis: A rotating aircraft rendered in typewriter glyphs.
options.viewport: An aircraft made of characters rotating under scroll.
options.case: Spectacular but says nothing about technical logs or signatures.
options.kept: One strict grid as the entire composition.

options.label: Silk Colour Chords
options.thesis: Overlapping silk lanes as computed colour states.
options.viewport: Horizontal lanes crossing a bright field.
options.case: No connection to aviation operations; abstract.

options.label: Luminescent Understory
options.thesis: Content glowing alive under the pointer.
options.viewport: A dark field lit by proximity.
options.kept: Reveal by proximity, used for field detail on hover.

canonCard.label: The category standard
canonCard.thesis: Aviation SaaS done impeccably: deep navy, iPad mockup, feature grid, sky photography.
canonCard.viewport: Headline left, iPad with the app right, logo strip below.
canonCard.risk: Indistinguishable from every MRO and EFB vendor by design.
